questions: Does progress on the s-bend stay at or above 0.155 (iteration 1 value) with the 16 mm footprint, or does it fall?
Do line_loss_events fall from 1 per run to 0, or stay at 1?
Is max_error still at or near 0.06 m, and at what progress does each run end?
Does steering_oscillation stay within 0.07 to 0.15, or does the larger footprint raise it?
Does rms_error stay near 0.03 on every track? A constant value would point to a motor-mismatch offset rather than a geometry limit.
feedback_request.requested_changes_if_any: If progress is unchanged and line losses remain at 1, say whether gains (kp or kd) or the line_loss setting would help more than a wider ±4 cm span. If progress falls below 0.11 on the oval, confirm the footprint is the cause before I test any further span change.

intent: Single-variable test from the best design (iteration 1). Restore the 4 cm lead (y = 0.04 m) that gave the best s-bend progress (0.155) and the best score (51.27), after the 2 cm lead dropped s-bend progress to 0.04. Keep the ±3 cm span, 5 sensors at 1.5 cm pitch, 0.6 kg mass, 0.11 m track and 0.03 m wheel radius unchanged, and change only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016 m. This isolates whether a larger footprint reduces the single line loss per run and the off-track exits. Expect line_loss_events near 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and s-bend progress of at least 0.15.
learning: Iteration 3 is the first clean lead test. A 2 cm lead cut s-bend progress from 0.155 to 0.04, and iteration 2 (3 cm lead, wider span) gave the same 0.04. Taken together, a lead below 4 cm appears to hurt the s-bend, so lead is not the limit at 4 cm. Span alone (±6 cm) removed line losses without fixing the off-track exits, so the remaining untested geometry variable is footprint at the 4 cm lead. Oscillation has stayed in 0.065-0.155 in every iteration, so jitter is not the limit. The rms_error near 0.03 on every track suggests a steady offset, which may come from the motor mismatch and is a gain question for the Integrator.
rationale: Race evidence: iteration 1 (±3 cm span, 5 sensors at 1.5 cm pitch, 12 mm footprints, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track) is the best design so far at 51.27. Its s-bend progress was 0.155. Iteration 3 changed only the lead, to 2 cm, and scored 25.37. Its s-bend progress fell to 0.04, and line losses stayed at 1 per run. The 2 cm lead is therefore worse, not better. Iteration 2 also gave s-bend progress of 0.04 with a 3 cm lead, so a short lead is consistently associated with the s-bend collapse. Widening the span to ±6 cm with 16 mm footprints (iteration 2) removed line losses but did not stop off-track exits. So neither span nor lead below 4 cm is the answer. The Integrator's feedback for iteration 3 asked for the decision rule: if progress falls, restore the 4 cm lead and test sensor_size 0.016 alone. Progress did fall, so I follow that rule. I restore the iteration 1 geometry exactly (±3 cm, 5 sensors, 4 cm lead, 0.6 kg, 0.11 m track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.12 m body) and change only sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016. Expected result: the larger footprint lets each sensor see more of the 25 mm tape at the ±3 cm extremes, so line losses should fall toward 0 without the wide-span penalty seen in iteration 2, and max_error should drop below about 0.06 m with s-bend progress at or above 0.15. Off-track exits are still expected to be the limit. If progress is unchanged and line losses remain at 1, the next candidate is a ±4 cm span at 16 mm. If progress falls again, the footprint is not the variable and the lead of 4 cm is the best geometry, so the remaining gap should be handled by the Integrator's gains.
